title: L01 Request lifecycle: a newer message retires a reply in preparation, and a stalled reply stops at the deadline
capability: While a reply is still being prepared the person may keep typing: the newer message is taken as an addition or a new subject, the older reply is never shown and never stored, and nothing the person said is lost. A reply whose Provider stalls is stopped at the request deadline with an honest timeout, commits nothing late and leaves nothing running, and the conversation carries on normally afterwards.

allowed.statement: The person's sibling joined the outing to the stalls and they shared a dessert on the kerb.
The person and the sibling floated a long autumn ridge walk that a parent used to lead.

forbidden.statement: Explaining the delay or the stopped request in system terms such as timeouts, streams or retries.

expectedBehavior: The reply to the addition answers the narrowed question and the earlier question is not lost.
The superseded reply never appears in history.
The stalled request ends with a plain timeout well inside the budget and the next message is answered normally.
failureSignals: A reply to a message the person already replaced appears on the screen or in history.
A stalled request keeps the person waiting past the budget or is answered late.
A command or attempt stays running after the request ended.

sourceEligibility.reason: Retained original expression inside the default background.

criteria.description: The reply to the message the person replaced is neither shown nor stored.
The addition commits as one complete reply and history matches the stream.
The earlier question the person replaced still reaches the Provider with the addition, so nothing they said is lost.
The original account of the outing reaches the Provider for the addition.
A stalled Provider ends with a timeout inside the budget, commits nothing late and leaves no command running.
The conversation continues normally after the stopped request.
